rules.coverage_text: All residential real property unless exempted.

exemptions.description: Housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years
Separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with corporate member, with notice
Duplex where owner occupies one unit

key_values.name: base_percent
key_values.text: 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living

key_values.name: max_increments
key_values.text: not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period

rules.penalty: Civil liability: injunctive relief, damages for excess rent, attorney's fees, up to three times damages if willful.
rules.quote: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
relations_hint: not intended to expand or limit the authority of local governments to establish local policies regulating rents consistent with Chapter 2.7
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the local CPI change, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. No more than two increases are allowed in 12 months for the same tenant.
tenancy_conditions: Initial rate for new tenancy not subject to cap
rules.title: Statewide rent cap
